text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Alexander Rezes, Minister of Transport, Post and Telecommunication, said he was considering resigning from his post because of health problems.

- Jan Luptak, leader of the junior coalition party, the ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), said a referendum on Slovakia's entry to European structures will be held in February 1997. Luptak said his party did not support the integration.

- Development and restructuring of the of transport, posts and telecom sectors will need overall investments of around 211.8 billion crowns by the year 2000. The sector will provide 47.8 billion from its own resources, domestic loans should total 42.2 billion, foreign loans should cover 21.9 billion crowns and state subsidies should total 34.9 billion.

- The opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said it would take the recently approved controversial law on bankruptcies, which prevents state companies from going into liquidation, to the constitutional court.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The proposed increase of a guaranteed price of unprocessed milk to 7.30 crowns will increase prices of milky products and may destabilise the relatively stable food market.

- Production in the cellulose and paper industry totalled 8.9 billion crowns in the first half of this year, a decrease of four percent compared with the same period last year. Sales totalled 9.5 billion crowns, some 4.7 percent less than in the first six months of 1995.
- Motor fuel distributor Aral Slovakia plans to build 15 petrol stations in Slovakia in the next three years, and account for about eight percent of the Slovak market.
SME - A congress of the Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) begins today.

- Three opposition parties, the Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), Democratic Union (DU) and Democratic Party (DS) said they would sign a cooperation agreement by the end of October. The agreement does not mean a joint candidate list for next elections.
